==Problem==
The taxi fare in Gotham City is <nowiki>$2.40</nowiki> for the first <math>\frac12</math> mile and additional mileage charged at the rate <nowiki>$0.20</nowiki> for each additional 0.1 mile. You plan to give the driver a <nowiki>$2</nowiki> tip. How many miles can you ride for <nowiki>$10</nowiki>?

<math> \textbf{(A) }3.0\qquad\textbf{(B) }3.25\qquad\textbf{(C) }3.3\qquad\textbf{(D) }3.5\qquad\textbf{(E) }3.75 </math>

==Solution 1 (Algebra)==
Let <math>x</math> be the number of miles you ride. The number of miles you ride after the first half mile is <math>x-0.5.</math> We can write this equation:



<cmath>\begin{align*} 10 &= 2.4 + 0.2 \times \frac{x-0.5}{0.1} + 2\\
5.6 &= 2(x-0.5)\\
2.8 &= x-0.5\\
x &= \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 3.3}\end{align*}</cmath>

==Solution 2 (Table)==

\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
Miles & Money & Remark\\
\hline
0 & 8 & \text{2  for  tip} \\
\hline
0.5 & 5.6 & \text{-2.4  for  first  0.5  mi} \\
\hline
3.3 & 0 & \text{-5.6  for  2.8  mi}
\end{array}

Miles travelled = <math>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 3.3}</math>
